summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of atrial fibrillation, dilated cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, morbid obesity, and prior strokes was admitted for lower abdominal pain and gross hematuria. He had a long-standing indwelling Foley catheter placed at his nursing home, which was removed upon admission, revealing significant debris. Imaging showed mild fat stranding around the bladder, suggestive of cystitis, and worsening stenosis of the proximal splenic artery, though vascular surgery did not recommend intervention. The abdominal pain and hematuria resolved during the hospital stay, likely due to catheter-related irritation. He was found to have acute kidney injury, likely pre-renal, which resolved with IV fluids. He failed a trial of void and required continued catheterization. Aspirin and ibuprofen were held due to bleeding risk and renal concerns. He was discharged to extended care with stable condition, plans for urology and neurology follow-up, and instructions to monitor kidney function and hematuria before resuming certain medications.
